## `bam::Status`

[source](bam.goose#L21-L30)

```goose
enum Status {
    Record,
    End,
    Invalid,
    Truncated,
    IoError,
    Closed,
    TooLarge,
    Unsorted,
}
```

Result of a BAM operation. read() returns Record when an alignment is ready
and End at normal end-of-file. open() and seek() also return Record on success,
but you must call read() before accessing an alignment after either operation.

Other values report failures. TooLarge means a configured size limit was
exceeded. Unsorted is reported by region-loading code when mapped records
go backward in coordinate order; the sequential reader does not check order.
After read() returns End or an error, further reads return that same status
until the reader is opened or successfully repositioned with seek().

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Closed);
```

<a id="api-2"></a>

## `bam::check`

[source](bam.goose#L50-L55)

```goose
fn check(actual: Status, expected: Status, message: const u8[:] = "BAM status mismatch") -> Status
```

Require an explicit expected status, returning the actual status on a match.
A mismatch aborts with the expected and actual names and optional context.
Abort is not catchable and does not run deferred cleanup. For recovery, use
the callback overload or inspect the status directly. End is not Record.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
reader.open("tests/data/example.bam").check(bam::Status.Record, "opening BAM");
reader.read().check(bam::Status.Record);
```

<a id="api-3"></a>

## `bam::check`

[source](bam.goose#L71-L74)

```goose
fn check<F: fn(Status)>(actual: Status, expected: Status) -> Status
```

Invoke the handler only on a mismatch. If it falls through, return the
original status unchanged; there is no automatic abort. A return inside an
inline block exits its enclosing named function and runs deferred cleanup.
A named handler returns normally to check instead.

```goose
var called = false;
let status = bam::Status.Closed.check(bam::Status.Record) { actual =>
    assert(actual == bam::Status.Closed);
    called = true;
};
assert(called && status == bam::Status.Closed);
bam::Status.End.check(bam::Status.End) { actual => assert(false); };
```

## `bam::Reference`

[source](bam.goose#L89-L93)

```goose
struct Reference {
    name:     i64,
    name_len: i64,
    length:   i64,
}
```

One reference sequence from the BAM header. Its position in
reader.references is its reference ID, also called tid.
name is a byte offset into reader.names, not the reference ID or a string.
name_len is the name's byte length; length is the reference length in bases.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let ref = reader.references[0];
assert(reader.names[ref.name..ref.name + ref.name_len] == "chrA");
assert(ref.length == 200000);
```

<a id="api-5"></a>

## `bam::Fields`

[source](bam.goose#L116-L133)

```goose
struct Fields {
    tid:           i32,
    pos:           i64,
    end:           i64,
    reference_len: i64,
    flags:         u16,
    mapq:          u8,
    mate_tid:      i32,
    mate_pos:      i64,
    template_len:  i32,
    name_len:      i64,
    cigar:         i64,
    cigar_len:     i64,
    seq:           i64,
    seq_len:       i64,
    qual:          i64,
    aux:           i64,
}
```

Decoded metadata for one alignment. tid is the reference's index in the BAM
header, and pos is the zero-based alignment start. end is exclusive: an
alignment overlaps [begin, stop) when pos < stop and end > begin.
reference_len counts reference bases consumed by the CIGAR operations.
For index overlap checks, end uses a minimum span of one even when the CIGAR
consumes no reference bases. tid, mate_tid, pos, and mate_pos use -1 when
the corresponding reference or position is missing.

cigar, seq, qual, and aux are byte offsets within this record, not file
offsets. Use Record.cigar(), base(), quality(), and aux() rather than
interpreting the packed data yourself. Do not construct this metadata by hand.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record);
let f = reader.record().fields;
assert(f.pos == 5 && f.end == 18 && f.reference_len == 13);
assert(f.seq_len == 13 && f.mate_tid == -1);
```

## `bam::Record`

[source](bam.goose#L147-L150)

```goose
struct Record {
    fields: Fields,
    bytes:  const u8[:],
}
```

A view of the current alignment in the reader's buffers; obtaining it does
not copy the record. Process it before the next read(), seek(), open(), or
close(), any of which invalidates its bytes. Copy any data you need to keep.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record);
let record = reader.record();
assert(record.name() == "match" && record.fields.tid == 0);
```

<a id="api-7"></a>

## `bam::Reader`

[source](bam.goose#L170-L183)

```goose
root struct Reader {
    stream:           bgzf::Reader,
    status:           Status         = Status.Closed,
    header:           u8[>..]        = [],
    names:            u8[>..]        = [],
    references:       Reference[>..] = [],
    bytes:            u8[>..]        = [],
    block_begin:      i64            = -1,
    fields:           Fields,
    data_start:       u64 = 0,
    max_record_bytes: i64 = 16777216,
    max_header_bytes: i64 = 16777216,
    max_references:   i64 = 1048576,
}
```

Reads one BAM alignment at a time, keeping the header and reference names
available throughout. Construct with Reader { .. }, open a BAM path, and
call read() followed by record(). Close the reader when finished.

BAM data is compressed in BGZF blocks. The reader decompresses blocks as
needed, without loading the whole file or genomic region. A record wholly
inside the current block refers directly to that buffer; a record spanning
blocks is assembled in reusable temporary storage.
Size limits guard against unexpectedly large input allocations and can be
raised before opening. Otherwise treat implementation fields as read-only.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
assert(reader.references.len == 2);
assert(reader.header[..3] == "@HD");
```

```goose
reader.close();
```

```goose
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record);
```

## `bam::tell`

[source](bam.goose#L259-L259)

```goose
fn tell(reader: const Reader&) -> u64
```

Virtual offset of the next alignment, usable with seek on this same BAM.
The low 16 bits are the uncompressed position inside a compressed BGZF block.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let start = reader.tell();
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record && reader.tell() > start);
```

<a id="api-11"></a>

## `bam::seek`

[source](bam.goose#L276-L283)

```goose
fn seek(reader: Reader&, offset: u64) -> Status
```

Seek to an alignment boundary obtained from tell or a matching BAM index.
Invalidates record views and resets EOF/errors, retaining the header. An
arbitrary byte offset is not an alignment boundary and may fail on read.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let start = reader.tell();
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record);
assert(reader.seek(start) == bam::Status.Record);
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record);
let record = reader.record();
assert(record.name() == "match");
```

## `bam::record`

[source](bam.goose#L347-L352)

```goose
fn record(reader: const Reader&) -> Record
```

Borrow the last successfully read record. Call only after read returns Record.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record);
let first = reader.record();
assert(first.name() == "match");
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record);
let second = reader.record();
assert(second.name() == "reverse"); // first's bytes are no longer valid.
```

<a id="api-14"></a>

## `bam::read`

[source](bam.goose#L368-L372)

```goose
fn read(reader: Reader&) -> Status
```

Read one alignment, reusing bytes. Record bytes are invalidated even when a
read fails. End and failures are sticky until open/seek. Records can span
many BGZF blocks.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
var count = 0;
var status = reader.read();
while status == bam::Status.Record { count += 1; status = reader.read(); }
assert(count == 21 && status == bam::Status.End);
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.End);
```

<a id="api-15"></a>

## `bam::records`

[source](bam.goose#L390-L398)

```goose
fn records<F: fn(const Record&)>(reader: Reader&) -> Status
```

Visit remaining records from the current position without copying them.
Each view expires on the next reader operation; do not reposition or close
the reader inside the callback. Returns Record on clean completion (even
when already at EOF), otherwise the read failure. Earlier callbacks are not
rolled back on failure. reader.status remains End after normal completion.
An inline callback can return from its enclosing function to stop early.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
reader.open("tests/data/example.bam").check(bam::Status.Record);
var count = 0;
let status = reader.records() { record => count += 1; };
status.check(bam::Status.Record);
assert(count == 21 && reader.status == bam::Status.End);
```

## `bam::cigar`

[source](bam.goose#L593-L596)

```goose
fn cigar(record: const Record&, index: i64) -> u32
```

CIGAR word, with length in its upper 28 bits and SAM operation in its low 4.
index must be in [0, fields.cigar_len). Long-CIGAR CG arrays are transparent.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record);
let record = reader.record();
assert(record.cigar(0) == 13 << 4); // 13M
```


<a id="api-21"></a>

## `bam_index::Chunk`

[source](bam_index.goose#L24-L27)

```goose
struct Chunk {
    begin: u64,
    end:   u64,
}
```

A candidate range of records in a BAM file. begin is inclusive and end is
exclusive. These are BGZF virtual offsets: the high 48 bits locate a
compressed block in the file, and the low 16 bits locate a byte inside the
decompressed block. They are not genomic coordinates or byte distances.

Call reader.seek(chunk.begin), then read records while reader.tell() is less
than chunk.end. Check each record's reference ID and alignment coordinates:
a chunk may include records outside the genomic region you requested.
A chunk describes where to read; it does not hold those records in memory.

```goose
let chunk = bam_index::Chunk { begin: 100, end: 200 };
assert(chunk.begin < chunk.end);
```

<a id="api-22"></a>

## `bam_index::Index`

[source](bam_index.goose#L58-L68)

```goose
root struct Index {
    references: Reference[>..] = [],
    bins:       Bin[>..]       = [],
    chunks:     Chunk[>..]     = [],
    linear:     u64[>..]       = [],
    min_shift:  i64            = 14,
    depth:      i64            = 5,
    csi:        bool           = false,
    status:     bam::Status    = bam::Status.Closed,
    max_bytes:  i64            = 268435456,
}
```

An in-memory BAM index, reusable across region queries. open reads a .bai or
.csi file and closes it after parsing. Both uncompressed and BGZF-compressed
index files are supported. Pass the index path, not the BAM path.

max_bytes limits the decompressed index input to 256 MiB by default; parsed
tables and temporary buffers require additional memory. Set this limit
before open and otherwise treat the fields as read-only.
BAI supports positions below 2^29. CSI can cover longer references; accepted
CSI headers have depth 0..10 and min_shift + 3*depth at most 62.

```goose
let index = bam_index::Index { .. };
assert(index.open("tests/data/example.bam.bai") == bam::Status.Record);
assert(index.references.len == 2);
```

<a id="api-23"></a>

## `bam_index::open`

[source](bam_index.goose#L109-L116)

```goose
fn open(index: Index&, path: const u8[:]) -> bam::Status
```

Replace the index. Failure clears any previous data; errors use bam::Status.
The index must belong to the BAM used for loading; the formats have no file
identity checksum, so a stale index cannot always be detected.

```goose
let index = bam_index::Index { .. };
assert(index.open("tests/data/example.bam.bai") == bam::Status.Record);
assert(index.open("") == bam::Status.IoError);
assert(index.references.len == 0);
```

<a id="api-24"></a>

## `bam_index::open_for`

[source](bam_index.goose#L129-L141)

```goose
fn open_for(index: Index&, bam_path: const u8[:]) -> bam::Status
```

Discover an adjacent index without opening the BAM. Try path + ".csi",
then replace a trailing ".bam" with ".csi", then the same two BAI names.
The first existing file wins; parsing or reading errors do not fall back.
No index is created. Missing indexes return IoError and clear old data.
Use open(index_path) to select an explicit index instead.

```goose
let index = bam_index::Index { .. };
index.open_for("tests/data/example.bam").check(bam::Status.Record);
assert(index.references.len == 2);
```

<a id="api-25"></a>

## `bam_index::query`

[source](bam_index.goose#L265-L314)

```goose
fn query(index: const Index&, tid: i32, begin: i64, end: i64, output: Chunk[>..]&) -> bam::Status
```

Find file ranges that may contain records overlapping one genomic region.
tid is the reference's zero-based index in the BAM header, not a name or
an offset into the header's name array. begin and end are zero-based genomic
coordinates: begin is included and end is excluded.

Replaces output with chunks sorted by file position, merging overlapping
ranges so the same file range is not visited twice within this query.
Separate queries can still return overlapping chunks. The chunks are only
candidates: after reading, keep records with the requested tid and with
record.fields.pos < end and record.fields.end > begin.

Returns Record on success, including an empty region with no chunks.
Invalid reference IDs or coordinates outside the index's range fail.
The index cannot determine whether its BAM file has changed since indexing.

```goose
let index = bam_index::Index { .. };
assert(index.open("tests/data/example.bam.bai") == bam::Status.Record);
var chunks: bam_index::Chunk[>..] = [];
assert(index.query(0, 5, 7, chunks) == bam::Status.Record && chunks.len > 0);
assert(index.query(0, 7, 7, chunks) == bam::Status.Record && chunks.len == 0);
```

<a id="api-26"></a>

## `bam_index::fetch`

[source](bam_index.goose#L342-L377)

```goose
fn fetch<F: fn(const bam::Record&)>(index: const Index&, reader: bam::Reader&,
        tid: i32, begin: i64, end: i64) -> bam::Status
```

Select and visit alignments overlapping [begin, end) on reference tid.
Coordinates are zero-based and half-open. Reuses the open reader and index,
including for backward queries or after EOF. Requires coordinate-sorted BAM
and a matching index. Sorting is checked only in the visited records.
Returns Record on completion, including empty results; failures may follow
earlier callbacks and do not undo their effects. Every visited record is
fully decoded and validated. Unlike pileup, no flag/MAPQ filters are applied:
positioned unmapped and zero-span records use BAM's minimum span of one.
Each record borrows reader storage until the next reader operation. Do not
read, seek, close or fetch on that reader inside the callback. An inline
return exits the enclosing function and permits stopping early.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
reader.open("tests/data/example.bam").check(bam::Status.Record);
let index = bam_index::Index { .. };
index.open_for("tests/data/example.bam").check(bam::Status.Record);
var count = 0;
let status = index.fetch(reader, 0 as i32, 5, 7) { record =>
    assert(record.name() == "match");
    count += 1;
};
status.check(bam::Status.Record);
assert(count == 1);
```

<a id="api-27"></a>

## `bam_index::fetch`

[source](bam_index.goose#L393-L396)

```goose
fn fetch<F: fn(const bam::Record&)>(index: const Index&, reader: bam::Reader&,
        name: const u8[:], begin: i64, end: i64) -> bam::Status
```

Fetch by reference name instead of ID. Unknown names return Invalid without
invoking the callback. All other behavior is the same as the tid overload.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
reader.open("tests/data/example.bam").check(bam::Status.Record);
let index = bam_index::Index { .. };
index.open_for("tests/data/example.bam").check(bam::Status.Record);

    assert(record.name() == "match");
};
status.check(bam::Status.Record);
```

<a id="api-28"></a>

## `pileup::Filter`

[source](pileup.goose#L28-L32)

```goose
struct Filter {
    exclude_flags:    u16  = 0x704,
    min_mapq:         u8   = 0,
    retain_zero_span: bool = false,
}
```

Choose which alignment records to keep when loading a region.
exclude_flags rejects a record when any of these SAM flag bits are set.
The default mask, 0x704, rejects unmapped, secondary, quality-control-failed,
and duplicate records. Supplementary alignments are kept.
min_mapq is the minimum mapping quality; it does not filter base qualities.
Overlapping mates are not combined when producing pileup positions.

Unmapped records are always skipped, even with exclude_flags set to zero.
By default, records whose CIGAR consumes no reference positions are also
skipped. Set retain_zero_span to keep those mapped records in input order,
for example when reproducing another tool's read-count limit. They remain
available through Store.record(), but do not contribute to pileup positions.

```goose
let filter = pileup::Filter { min_mapq: 20, .. };
assert(filter.exclude_flags == 0x704 && filter.min_mapq == 20);
```

<a id="api-29"></a>

## `pileup::SlimRecord`

[source](pileup.goose#L51-L72)

```goose
struct SlimRecord {
    tid:           i32,
    pos:           i64,
    end:           i64,
    reference_len: i64,
    flags:         u16,
    mapq:          u8,
    mate_tid:      i32,
    mate_pos:      i64,
    template_len:  i32,
    name:          u32,
    name_len:      u32,
    cigar:         u32,
    cigar_len:     u32,
    seq:           u32,
    seq_len:       u32,
    qual:          u32,
    aux:           u32,
    aux_len:       u32,
    // Index in Store.records of the matched mate, or -1 if no mate was linked.
    mate_index: i64 = -1,
}
```

Metadata for one stored alignment. tid is its reference's index in the BAM
header. pos is the zero-based alignment start; end is the exclusive end.

Variable-length data lives in separate arrays owned by Store. The name,
cigar, seq, qual, and aux fields are offsets into those arrays, not file
positions. Offsets and lengths count array elements: bytes for names, bases,
qualities, and tags; u32 operations for CIGARs. Use Store.record() to access
those values without calculating the array slices yourself.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let store = pileup::Store { .. };
assert(store.load(reader, 0, 5, 7) == bam::Status.Record);
assert(store.records[0].pos == 5 && store.records[0].seq_len == 13);
```

<a id="api-30"></a>

## `pileup::Store`

[source](pileup.goose#L108-L122)

```goose
root struct Store {
    records:          SlimRecord[>..] = [],
    names:            u8[>..]         = [],
    bases:            u8[>..]         = [],
    cigars:           u32[>..]        = [],
    qualities:        u8[>..]         = [],
    auxiliary:        u8[>..]         = [],
    mate_stats:       MateLinkStats   = MateLinkStats { .. },
    tid:              i32             = -1,
    begin:            i64             = 0,
    end:              i64             = 0,
    max_bytes:        i64             = 4294967295,
    retain_auxiliary: bool            = true,
    auto_link_mates:  bool            = true,
}
```

Owns all records loaded for one genomic region. Loading another region
replaces those records while reusing the allocated storage.

Names, unpacked base codes, CIGAR operations, base qualities, and raw
auxiliary tags each occupy a separate growable array. These arrays are also
called slabs: each holds one kind of data for every record in the region.
Each base code is a byte from 0 to 15; record.base() converts it to a letter.
The original packed BAM records are not kept. Header data belongs to the
reader, but the stored records remain usable after that reader closes.

max_bytes limits the combined bytes in the five data arrays. It does not
include record metadata, spare allocation capacity, or other readers and
workers. Its default and hard upper bound are 2^32-1 bytes (4 GiB minus one),
so the u32 offsets into these arrays remain representable. The arrays grow
as needed; setting the limit does not allocate that much memory. Exceeding
the limit fails the load instead of returning a partial set of records.
Set max_bytes before loading. retain_auxiliary=false omits optional BAM tags
from stored records; record.aux() then returns an empty slice. CIGARs using
the CG tag are still resolved before storage. auto_link_mates=false skips
finding primary mate pairs: mate_index remains -1 and mate_stats stays zero
until you explicitly call link_mates(). Both options default to true and
survive store reuse. Otherwise treat the fields as read-only.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let store = pileup::Store { .. };
assert(store.load(reader, 0, 5, 7) == bam::Status.Record);
assert(store.records.len == 1);
reader.close(); // Stored records own their bytes, independently of Reader.
let record = store.record(0);
assert(record.name() == "match");
```

```goose
    cigar_words:   const u32[:],
    quality_bytes: const u8[:],
    aux_bytes:     const u8[:],
}
```

A view of one alignment owned by Store. Its slices refer to the store's
arrays rather than copying their contents. Closing the BAM reader does not
invalidate this view; loading, clearing, or modifying the store does.
Copy any data you need to keep before reusing the store for another region.

```goose

let store = pileup::Store { .. };

assert(record.fields.seq_len == record.bases.len);
```

## `pileup::MateLinkStats`

[source](pileup.goose#L260-L260)

```goose
struct MateLinkStats { pairs: i64 = 0, ambiguous_qnames: i64 = 0 }
```

Results of Seqair-style mate linking. pairs counts reciprocal links;
ambiguous_qnames counts eligible records without a free reciprocal partner
when another eligible record of that name was already seen. It is a record
count, not a count of distinct names. Inspect nonzero ambiguity explicitly.

```goose
let store = pileup::Store { .. };
let stats = store.link_mates();
assert(stats.pairs == 0 && stats.ambiguous_qnames == 0);
```

<a id="api-39"></a>

## `pileup::link_mates`

[source](pileup.goose#L278-L314)

```goose
fn link_mates(store: Store&) -> MateLinkStats
```

Link primary mapped pairs already in the store, using equal name bytes,
same-reference mate fields and reciprocal positions (not READ1/READ2 bits).
Secondary/supplementary, unmapped/mate-unmapped and empty-name records are
excluded. No outside-region mate fetch or overlap correction is performed.
Loaders call this after loading when Store.auto_link_mates is true (default).
Calling again is idempotent;
reordering/removing records requires relinking before reading mate_index.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let store = pileup::Store { .. };
assert(store.load(reader, 0, 5, 7) == bam::Status.Record);
assert(store.link_mates().pairs == 0 && store.records[0].mate_index == -1);
```

<a id="api-40"></a>

## `pileup::load`

[source](pileup.goose#L338-L356)

```goose
fn load<R>(store: Store&, reader: R&, tid: i32, begin: i64, end: i64,
        filter: Filter = Filter { .. }) -> bam::Status
```

Read forward and retain alignments overlapping [begin, end) on reference tid.
tid is the reference's index in the BAM header; coordinates are zero-based,
with end excluded. Requires coordinate-sorted input and a freshly opened
reader for each independent query.
Returns Record on success, including an empty region. Error clears the store.
This is not an indexed query: it reads preceding records and consumes the
first mapped record beyond the region. Reopen before a different query.
Unsorted detects decreasing mapped coordinates only in the scanned prefix;
it cannot validate the unvisited remainder of a file. Empty regions do no I/O.
Set store.retain_auxiliary=false to omit optional tags from retained records,
or store.auto_link_mates=false to skip finding their primary mate partners.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let store = pileup::Store { .. };
assert(store.load(reader, reader.reference_id("chrA"), 5, 7) == bam::Status.Record);
assert(store.records.len == 1);
assert(store.load(reader, 0, 9, 8) == bam::Status.Invalid);
assert(store.records.len == 0 && store.bases.len == 0);
```

<a id="api-41"></a>

## `pileup::load_indexed`

[source](pileup.goose#L393-L410)

```goose
fn load_indexed(store: Store&, reader: bam::Reader&, index: const bam_index::Index&,
                tid: i32, begin: i64, end: i64, filter: Filter = Filter { .. }) -> bam::Status
```

Use a matching BAM index to load alignments overlapping [begin, end).
tid is the reference's index in the BAM header; coordinates are zero-based,
with end excluded. Reuses the open reader, index and allocated record arrays,
including backward queries and queries after EOF. No prefix scan or reopen.
Set store.retain_auxiliary=false to omit optional tags from retained records,
or store.auto_link_mates=false to skip finding their primary mate partners.
Like Seqair, rejects non-overlapping/filtered raw records before full decode.
BGZF and record framing are always checked; names/auxiliary/query lengths
of discarded records are not validated. Retained records are fully checked.
Invalidates the reader's record view; call read before borrowing it again.
Failures clear the store. Sorting is checked only in visited chunks; indexes
cannot prove that the BAM is sorted, complete, or unchanged since indexing.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let index = bam_index::Index { .. };
assert(index.open("tests/data/example.bam.bai") == bam::Status.Record);
let store = pileup::Store { .. };
assert(store.load_indexed(reader, index, 0, 95, 100) == bam::Status.Record);
assert(store.load_indexed(reader, index, 0, 5, 7) == bam::Status.Record);
{
    let record = store.record(0);
    assert(store.records.len == 1 && record.name() == "match");
}
assert(store.load_indexed(reader, index, 0, 0, 30,
    pileup::Filter { retain_zero_span: true, .. }) == bam::Status.Record);
var empty = 0;
for record in store.records { if record.reference_len == 0 { empty += 1; } }
assert(empty == 3); // Empty CIGAR, insertion-only, soft-clip-only.
store.columns() { pos, entries =>
    for entry in entries { assert(store.records[entry.record_index].reference_len > 0); }
};
```

<a id="api-42"></a>

## `pileup::pileup`

[source](pileup.goose#L436-L442)

```goose
fn pileup<F: fn(i64, const Entry[:])>(store: Store&, reader: bam::Reader&,
        index: const bam_index::Index&, tid: i32, begin: i64, end: i64,
        filter: Filter = Filter { .. }) -> bam::Status
```

Load an indexed region and visit its covered positions. The callback gets
a zero-based position and entries borrowed for that call; store.record()
accesses contributing reads. Uses load_indexed's filters, mate linking and
storage options. A failed load clears the store and invokes no callbacks.
Returns Record on success, including empty regions. Do not reload or mutate
the store inside the callback. Repeated queries reuse its storage.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
reader.open("tests/data/example.bam").check(bam::Status.Record);
let index = bam_index::Index { .. };
index.open_for("tests/data/example.bam").check(bam::Status.Record);
let store = pileup::Store { .. };
var count = 0;
let status = store.pileup(reader, index, 0 as i32, 5, 7) { pos, entries =>
    assert(pos == 5 + count && entries.len == 1);
    let record = store.record(entries[0].record_index);
    assert(record.name() == "match");
    count += 1;
};
status.check(bam::Status.Record);
assert(count == 2);
```

## `pileup::Entry`

[source](pileup.goose#L641-L644)

```goose
struct Entry {
    record_index: i64, qpos: i64, base: u8, quality: u8,
    op:           Op, indel: i64,

```

record_index indexes Store.records. qpos is -1 for deletion/skip or absent
sequence; base is 'N' and quality 255 when unavailable. indel is anchored at

Sequence remains in BAM's stored orientation, including reverse-strand reads.

```goose
let store = pileup::Store { .. };
assert(store.load(reader, 0, 5, 6) == bam::Status.Record);
store.columns() { pos, entries =>
    assert(pos == 5 && entries.len == 1);
    let e = entries[0];
    assert(e.qpos == 0 && e.base == 'A' && e.quality == 13);
    assert(e.op == pileup::Op.Base && e.indel == 0);
};
```

<a id="api-48"></a>

## `pileup::columns`

[source](pileup.goose#L725-L772)

```goose
fn columns<F: fn(i64, const Entry[:])>(store: const Store&)
```

Visit covered positions in [store.begin, store.end), in order. The callback
receives a zero-based position and a borrowed slice valid for that call only.
Column entries preserve input order. Scratch storage is reused; CIGAR cursors
only move forward. No reference FASTA, BAQ, mate dedup or depth cap is applied.
Only reference-consuming CIGAR operations produce entries; clips/insertions
alone never create columns. Empty positions are omitted, not zero-filled.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let store = pileup::Store { .. };
assert(store.load(reader, 0, 5, 7) == bam::Status.Record);
var count = 0;
store.columns() { pos, entries =>
    assert(pos == 5 + count && entries.len == 1);
    count += 1;
};
assert(count == 2);
```

[source](bam_encode.goose#L26-L32)

```goose
struct Alignment {
    name: const u8[:] = "*",
    tid: i32 = -1, pos: i64 = -1, flags: u16 = 0, mapq: u8 = 0,
    mate_tid: i32 = -1, mate_pos: i64 = -1, template_len: i32 = 0,
```

Caller-owned alignment data. Sequence is ASCII IUPAC in stored orientation;
qualities are raw Phred bytes (empty means missing), CIGARs are native BAM
words, and aux contains raw BAM tags. -1 means absent reference/position.
No input is retained by encode or write. Empty sequence means absent SEQ.

```goose

let alignment = bam_encode::Alignment { name: "read", tid: 0, pos: 4,
    cigar: cigar, sequence: "aN", .. };

assert(bytes.len > 32);
```

[source](bam_encode.goose#L47-L52)

Encode a BAM payload (without block_size) into reusable caller storage.

```goose

    sequence: "ACN", .. };
var bytes: u8[>..] = [];
assert(bam_encode::encode(alignment, bytes, 0) == bam::Status.Record);
```

[source](bam_writer.goose#L19-L25)

```goose
root struct Writer {

    references: i64 = 0,
    max_record_bytes: i64 = 16777216,
```

Owns one output and its compressor. Construct with Writer { .. }, open,

<a id="api-52"></a>

## `bam_writer::close`

[source](bam_writer.goose#L36-L43)

```goose
fn close(writer: Writer&) -> bam::Status
```

Flush/finish, close the OS handle and release the compressor. Check the
result; deferred cleanup alone cannot report a failed final write. A poisoned
output is closed without an EOF marker. Repeated close succeeds.

```goose
let writer = bam_writer::Writer { .. };
```

[source](sam.goose#L67-L94)

```goose

```

Open and read leading header lines, preserving the first alignment for
read(). Empty/header-only files open successfully. Errors close the input.

```goose
let path = "tests/data/doc.sam";
assert(write_file(path, "@SQ\tSN:chrA\tLN:100\nr\t0\tchrA\t6\t40\t4M\t*\t0\t0\tACGT\tIIII\n"));
defer delete_file(path);
let reader = sam::Reader { .. };

assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record);
let record = reader.record();
assert(record.name() == "r" && record.fields.pos == 5);
assert(record.base(2) == 'G' && record.quality(2) == 40);
assert(reader.open(path) == bam::Status.Record);
let store = pileup::Store { .. };
assert(store.load(reader, 0, 6, 8) == bam::Status.Record);

store.columns() { pos, entries => assert(entries.len == 1); columns += 1; };
assert(columns == 2);
```


Owns the input, reusable codec scratch and decoded slice slabs. Header and
reference names live until open; records live until the next read/open/close.
Limits bound individual containers, decoded blocks/slabs and records, not
total process memory. End/errors are sticky until open or seek_slice.

```goose

assert(reader.status == bam::Status.Closed);
```


Open CRAM 3.0/3.1 and decode its SAM header. Record means ready, not a read.

and XZ blocks require system libbz2/liblzma; missing codecs return Invalid

<a id="api-67"></a>

## `cram::seek_slice`

[source](cram.goose#L422-L446)

```goose
fn seek_slice<R>(reader: Reader&, container_offset: i64, slice_offset: i64, size: i64, source: R&) -> bam::Status
```

Seek to and decode one CRAI slice. container_offset is an absolute file byte
offset; slice_offset is relative to container data, not its header. size must
match the landmark span. Header/reference metadata survives; borrowed records
do not. Reuses the compressed container when adjacent queries share it.
source has the same contract as read. Use cram_index::Cursor for region reads.

```goose
let reader = cram::Reader { .. }; let source = ExampleReference { .. };
assert(reader.seek_slice(0, 0, 0, source) == bam::Status.Closed);
```

<a id="api-68"></a>

## `cram::read`

[source](cram.goose#L461-L488)

```goose
fn read<R>(reader: Reader&, source: R&) -> bam::Status
```

Read one record, reconstructing its entire slice before resolving mates.
source.fetch(name, begin, end, output) must replace output with exactly the
requested zero-based half-open reference window and return true on success.
An adapter can use goose-bio faidx::Reader; no FASTA dependency is imposed.
Reference bases are uppercased and nonzero single-reference MD5s checked.
Embedded/no-reference slices bypass source. Fetch failures and checked MD5
mismatches fail; multi-reference/zero-MD5 slices cannot verify FASTA identity.

```goose
let reader = cram::Reader { .. };
let source = ExampleReference { .. };
assert(reader.read(source) == bam::Status.Closed);
```

```goose
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let writer = cram_writer::Writer { .. }; defer writer.close();
let path = "tests/data/writer.cram"; defer delete_file(path);
assert(writer.open(path, reader.header, reader.references, reader.names) == bam::Status.Record);
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record);
let record = reader.record();
assert(writer.write(record) == bam::Status.Record);
assert(writer.close() == bam::Status.Record);
let input = cram::Reader { .. }; defer input.close();
let reference = ExampleReference {};
assert(input.open(path) == bam::Status.Record && input.read(reference) == bam::Status.Record);
let decoded = input.record();
assert(decoded.name() == "match");
```

<a id="api-86"></a>

## `cram_writer::write`

[source](cram_writer.goose#L302-L365)

```goose
fn write<T>(writer: Writer&, record: const T&) -> bam::Status
```

Encode a validated BAM/slab record. CIGAR =/X normalize to M and adjacent
equal operations coalesce, as CRAM decoders do. Names, bases, qualities, tags
and detached mate fields are retained. Unsupported inputs (including mapped
records without a usable CIGAR, unmapped CIGAR/nonzero MAPQ, cF/d tags and
unpaired records carrying a mate target) fail instead of silently losing data.

```goose
let writer = cram_writer::Writer { .. };
let alignment = bam_encode::Alignment { flags: 4, .. };
assert(writer.write(alignment) == bam::Status.Closed);
```
